dialect_only.reason: SQLite needs no change: its VARCHAR columns carry no fixed encoding, so the ciphertext a webhook secret stores (invalid UTF-8 almost by construction) is already accepted there, and PostgreSQL only needed the column converted to BYTEA.

dialect_only_set.reason: The set belongs to the PostgreSQL LISTEN/NOTIFY event-bus implementation itself; there is no SQLite sibling backend, so no other dialect has a schema to ship.
The set belongs to the PostgreSQL-implementation KV store itself; there is no SQLite sibling backend, so no other dialect has a schema to ship.

divergent.reason: The append-only backstop is a language-level construct with no shared spelling: SQLite uses a BEFORE UPDATE/DELETE trigger whose body raises through RAISE(ABORT, ...), PostgreSQL a plpgsql function raising an exception plus three triggers (it also covers TRUNCATE, which SQLite's trigger syntax cannot).

SQLite cannot ALTER a column's nullability, so making retry_after NOT NULL is a whole table rebuild there (recreate, copy, drop, rename, re-create both indexes); PostgreSQL is a single ALTER COLUMN SET NOT NULL. Both sides share the same idempotent backfill ahead of the enforcement and end schema-identical.
SQLite cannot ALTER a column type, so widening the three key_ref columns to VARCHAR(4096) rebuilds each table on that dialect; PostgreSQL is three ALTER COLUMN TYPE statements.
